fieldNotes.location: Roster coord (36.769855,-76.542823, movedMeters 5887) is a stale geocode and lands in trees NE of the actual building. Resolved to the very large single rectangular DC at ~36.7672,-76.5448 — bounded by a divided highway (Holland Rd / Rt 58 corridor) on the south, Progress Road and a rail spur on the north, and a creek/pond on the west. Confirmed PFG: Street View on the south frontage and along Progress Road repeatedly shows Performance Foodservice-branded delivery trucks (red/white 'Performance' logo, 800-849-7110) parked at and driving past this building. Address 1201 Progress Rd, Suffolk VA (operating entity Reinhart Foodservice LLC).
fieldNotes.buildingSize: Building is unusually large for a single broadline DC (~600k+ sq ft footprint). It may be a large multi-use warehouse with PFG as the dominant/primary tenant — flagged as a size uncertainty; trailer rows and PFG trucks confirm active foodservice DC operations.
fieldNotes.truckGate: No barrier arm or sliding gate seen in any Street View pass along Progress Road or the divided highway. North-side access driveways off Progress Road are open; a perimeter screening fence runs along the south but the truck entrances themselves appear uncontrolled. Classed false (open-access broadline pattern), but listed uncertain — trees obscure the exact NE entrance.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No guard booth structure visible at any entrance. A round white structure at the SW is a water tank, not a booth.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Long dock bank along the north face with ~50+ trailers backed in; banded 50+.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Extensive trailer parking — rows along the west/SW edge plus a north-side lot; 50+ trailers, banded 50+.
fieldNotes.railServed: A rail spur runs along the north property line into the site — railServed true.
fieldNotes.entryExitSeparate: Two separate driveways off Progress Road (NE and N) plus circulation; classed entry/exit separate, low confidence.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Edge-of-town Suffolk industrial park beside a residential subdivision and marshland — judged Rural per the rubric tie-break.
